title: fix(doctor): set aside allowlists for removed channel accounts instead of stopping migration
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Doctor stops later state migrations when a leftover channel allowlist belongs to an account removed from configuration.

Closes #134570. Thanks @oshunter for reporting the removed-account failure.

## User Impact

Doctor, including update-time repair, preserves the old allowlist in the existing `.migrated` archive (numbered on collision), warns with the source and archive paths, and continues. Malformed configured-account files and ambiguous account identities retain their existing refusal behavior. Authorization is never transferred to another account.

## Why This Change Was Made

The channel-pairing migration now distinguishes accounts absent from completed discovery from unresolved identities. It reuses the existing archive owner while retaining each source file, including identical duplicates. Recoverable orphan warnings cannot mask a separate configured-account refusal. Encoded identity matches remain unresolved across overlapping channel prefixes.

No schema, dependency, configuration, or CLI changes are needed. The existing update backup and rollback owners remain responsible for recovery.

## Evidence

- CI correction: `migrateLegacyChannelPairingState` declares `{ changes: string[]; warnings: string[]; warningDisposition?: "recoverable" }` inline, removing the type-import cycle locally. Shared type definitions and consumers remain unchanged, and the PR diff contains only its original four files. No barrel or lint exception was added.
- `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-madge-import-cycles.ts`: the PR-introduced channel-pairing cycle is gone; **0 new cycles** remain. The local count fell from 2 to 1. The remaining prepared-model-catalog fingerprint/worker cycle is unchanged from the base and already fixed upstream in [80bfd0f501b9](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/80bfd0f501b9e756b36ad1bfe634f914690c7be0); the local command still exits 1 for that inherited cycle.
- After the local return-type correction, the channel-pairing suite passed all 14 tests (25.28 seconds wall, 1.35 seconds test time). Core typechecking and scoped lint passed.
- All three removed-account regressions fail on the original migration code. An additional overlapping-prefix regression failed on the first candidate and passes after the matching correction.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/state-migrations.channel-pairing.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 14 tests passed on each of three runs; wall time 13.42 / 14.00 / 12.38 seconds, with 1.63 / 1.74 / 1.86 seconds of test time.
- Before consolidating the regression, the full Doctor migration flow passed with both the reported Feishu orphan and the mixed malformed-configured-account case. The broader two-file run passed 34 tests. The committed regressions use the real detection, migration, receipt, and step execution owners; each new case now takes less than one second instead of cold-loading unrelated Doctor/plugin owners.
- Three archive-consumer suites passed: 43 tests, 297.57 seconds wall time and 213.22 seconds of test time. The existing `state-migrations.recoverable-legacy-state.test.ts` accounts for 184.05 seconds of test time; its slow coverage is recorded under the campaign's local-proof exception.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` passed its ratchets, formatting, documentation, core types and all 27 test-type graphs, then failed its dead-export scan on `bindCliQuestionAnswerAuthority`, `prepareSessionEventTargetForHost`, `readSessionEntryCreationTransition`, and `RESTART_CONTINUATION_CONTEXT_PREFIX`. The maintainer confirmed that these identical failures reproduce on the unchanged base; this is inherited main red tracked separately from this fix. The remaining scoped lint, schema, storage, runtime import-cycle, webhook, and pairing checks passed individually. The initial runtime-only cycle check did not catch the type-import cycle subsequently reported by CI. Full-gate wall time: 834.24 seconds.
- P1 review attempts produced no verdict: the original attempt exited 1 after HTTP 401, and the latest inline-type correction review timed out after 120 seconds. Lead review remains pending under the approved review exception.
- All state proof used isolated homes/state directories. No live Gateway was touched. Hosted CI timing is pending at this authoring handoff.

Cumulative numstat: production **+38 / −7**, tests **+78 / −6**, docs **+8 / −0**; total **+124 / −13** across the original four files.
